name: Macroplastique pivotal trial
question: Does transurethral Macroplastique achieve at least noninferior continence improvement compared with Contigen in women with stress incontinence due primarily to intrinsic sphincter deficiency?

design.population: Adult women with stress urinary incontinence primarily due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency after unsuccessful conservative treatment.
design.locator: Full text, Study Design, pp 205–206; Figure 1, p 206

verdictNote: The paper’s treated-as-randomized Stamey analysis met its 15-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: In women with stress incontinence primarily due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency, Macroplastique improved Stamey grade in 75/122 (61.5%) versus 60/125 (48.0%) Contigen recipients at 12 months (difference 13.5 points; noninferiority P < 0.001); dryness was 45/122 (36.9%) versus 31/125 (24.8%).

reports.label: Pivotal comparison
reports.citation: Ghoniem G, Corcos J, Comiter C, et al. "Cross-Linked Polydimethylsiloxane Injection for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence: Results of a Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Single-Blind Study." *J Urol.* 2009;181(1):204-210. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.09.032
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Design, p 205; Outcome Measures, p 205

results.measure: At least one Stamey-grade improvement 12 months after last injection; paper-defined intent-to-treat set of 247 treated as randomized, with discontinuations counted as failures
results.note: Macroplastique-minus-Contigen difference, 13.5 percentage points. The paper states that the 95% upper bound for Contigen minus Macroplastique was below zero, without printing its numeric limit.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 206; Results, p 207; Table 3 and footnote, p 208

results.measure: Stamey grade 0 at 12 months after last injection; paper-defined intent-to-treat set of 247 treated as randomized, with discontinuations counted as failures
results.note: Nominal chi-square P < 0.05; the paper specifies no prespecified secondary-endpoint success threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote, p 208

results.measure: Mean one-hour pad-weight reduction from baseline at 12 months among follow-up attendees
results.note: Followed analysis; nominal between-arm P = 0.64. No prespecified secondary-endpoint success threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote, p 208

results.measure: Mean I-QOL score improvement from baseline at 12 months among follow-up attendees
results.note: Followed analysis; nominal between-arm P = 0.49. No prespecified secondary-endpoint success threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote, p 208

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Transurethral endoscopic implantation with a rigid 12-degree lens cystoscope; approximately 5 mL through a 5 Fr or 7 Fr needle under local or general anesthesia, occasionally with mild sedation; Macroplastique used an injector device.

delivery.label: Repeat injection
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Design, p 205; Table 2, p 207; Discussion, p 210
delivery.note: A second treatment was permitted after the 3-month visit; the protocol limited retreatment to one injection within four weeks of that visit.

delivery.label: Implant volume

values.exp: First 4.6 ± 1.2 mL; second 4.3 ± 1.4 mL; overall 6.8 ± 2.6 mL
values.ctl: First 4.6 ± 2.1 mL; second 4.5 ± 1.6 mL; overall 7.2 ± 3.5 mL

delivery.note: Means ± SD; second-treatment means are among recipients of a second injection.

results.note: Primary followed analysis; no prespecified success threshold or hypothesis test. Eight of 75 responders withdrew.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1445; Figure 3 and Results, p 1446

results.note: Of 38 women dry at 12 months, 33 remained dry; 12 of 29 improved but not dry became dry by 24 months. No prespecified threshold.

values.exp: 56/75 (74.7%) with withdrawals as failures; 64/75 (85.3%) with last observation carried forward

results.note: Sensitivity analyses of attrition; neither is the primary followed analysis.

values.exp: 53/67 (79.1%); mean 24 g at baseline and 4 g at both 12 and 24 months

results.note: No prespecified threshold; 54/67 (80.6%) had at least 50% reduction at 12 months.

harms.label: Genitourinary adverse events, months 12–24

values.exp: Among 67 followed responders, 4 women had 6 urinary tract infection events during months 12–24; no treatment- or device-related adverse events were reported

harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 1447
harms.note: Table 2 prints 3.3% for 4 affected women, corresponding mathematically to 122 initially treated; 67 responders were followed.

delivery.label: Retreatment, injection volume, and anesthesia in followed responders
delivery.value: 33/67 (49.3%) received repeat treatment at 3 months; mean first and second treatment volumes were 4.5 and 4.3 mL, mean total volume 6.6 mL per patient; local anesthesia was used for 73% of treatments.
